title: Nadia Lovell: Equities Must Earn the Next Leg Up
summary: As stocks rise and bond yields pull back ahead of the jobs report, Nadia Lovell of UBS says she remains bullish on equities, but believes the market’s next advance must be earned. She argues that markets are entering a new investment cycle after years of companies prioritizing financial efficiency through measures such as buybacks and lower capital spending. The shift now extends beyond AI to investment in power, supply chains, and defense, broadening corporate profit opportunities. If these investments deliver a productivity boost, Lovell says, they could support a healthier market and further gains over the longer term. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Job Growth Falls Short of Forecasts

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: See 'Skittishness' Around Credit: Annie Seelaus
summary:
Annie Seelaus, CEO of R. Seelaus, and John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson, join Emily Graffeo on "Bloomberg Real Yield." The spread on the riskiest US corporate bonds has jumped above 1,000 basis points over Treasuries for the first time since the regional banking crisis in 2023. That level of risk premium typically implies high probability of default, restructuring or loss.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bond Market Selloff in ‘New Chapter,’ JPM’s Berro Says

(Source: Bloomberg)
